proposals.before: His great-grandfather Sagisi had been tutor to the Prince of Liao, and Emperor Shizu had praised his virtue.
proposals.after: His grandfather Sagisi had been tutor to the Prince of Liao, and Emperor Shizu had praised his virtue.
proposals.reason: Chinese 大父 denotes the paternal grandfather, not the great-grandfather (曾祖); the idiomatic English overgenerates the kinship degree.

proposals.before: His great-grandfather Sagisi served as tutor to the Prince of Liao; the Shizu Emperor praised his worth.
proposals.after: His grandfather Sagisi served as tutor to the Prince of Liao; the Shizu Emperor praised his worth.
proposals.reason: Literal English should match 大父 as paternal grandfather rather than great-grandfather.

proposals.before: In 1346 he was promoted to right chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, then transferred to Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy.
proposals.after: In 1346 he was promoted to right chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, then transferred to Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts.
proposals.reason: 翰林學士承旨 is Recipient of Edicts (承旨), not Expositor-in-Chief (侍講/侍讀).

proposals.before: In the sixth year of Zhizheng he was promoted to Right Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, then changed to Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy.
proposals.after: In the sixth year of Zhizheng he was promoted to Right Chancellor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, then changed to Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts.
proposals.reason: Literal rendering misidentifies 承旨 as Expositor-in-Chief.

proposals.before: In 1347 he was transferred to vice censor-in-chief of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat at the age of sixty-nine.
proposals.after: In 1347 he was transferred to vice censor-in-chief of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate at the age of sixty-nine.
proposals.reason: 陝西行臺 is the Branch Censorate (行臺), not a Branch Secretariat (行省).

proposals.before: In the seventh year of Zhizheng he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat; he was then sixty-nine years old.
proposals.after: In the seventh year of Zhizheng he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate; he was then sixty-nine years old.
proposals.reason: Literal English wrongly maps 行臺 to Branch Secretariat.

proposals.before: His great-grandfather Guiyu served the Taizu Emperor and was officer in charge of the qielian kou qieshi.
proposals.after: His great-grandfather Guiyu served the Taizu Emperor and was officer in charge of the qielian households of the keshig.
proposals.reason: Literal English leaves qielian kou qieshi as unresolved transcription of 怯怜口怯薛官.

proposals.before: Temuder then had Yuelutiemuer appointed vice commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Office, demoting him from vice director of the palace to gentleman for managing affairs; within a month salt revenue increased by tens of thousands.
proposals.after: Temuder then had Yuelutiemuer appointed vice commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Office, demoting him from Lesser Grand Master of the Palace (yazhong daifu) to gentleman for managing affairs; within a month salt revenue increased by tens of thousands.
proposals.reason: Yazhong daifu (亚中大夫) is a rank title, not vice director of the palace.

proposals.before: Temuder then memorialized appointing Yuelutiemuer Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Office, demoting him from Vice Director of the Palace to Gentleman for Managing Affairs; within a month salt revenue increased by tens of thousands.
proposals.after: Temuder then memorialized appointing Yuelutiemuer Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Salt Transport Office, demoting him from Lesser Grand Master of the Palace to Gentleman for Managing Affairs; within a month salt revenue increased by tens of thousands.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 亚中大夫 as an office rather than the rank title.

proposals.before: In the second year of Zhizheng he came to audience; the emperor wished to retain him; he declined because his mother's funeral had not yet been buried.
proposals.after: In the second year of Zhizheng he came to audience; the emperor wished to retain him; he declined because his mother had not yet been buried.
proposals.reason: Literal English unnaturally makes the funeral the thing buried; 母丧未葬 means the deceased mother had not yet been buried.

proposals.before: When Buyantemuer arrived, they advanced together.
proposals.after: When Buyantiemuer arrived, they advanced together.
proposals.reason: Literal English misspells the biography subject's established name Buyantiemuer as Buyantemuer.

proposals.before: Before long Jiang Prefecture fell again and Xingji was killed.
proposals.after: Before long Jiang Prefecture fell again and Xingji died there.
proposals.reason: Chinese 死之 states that Xingji died there when the prefecture fell; idiomatic 'was killed' adds an unstated manner of death.

proposals.before: Buyantemuer convened the generals and said: "The bandits are linked inside and out; if we wait until they finish building fortifications and live off the grain of the various counties, defeating them will truly be difficult.
proposals.after: Buyantiemuer convened the generals and said: "The bandits are linked inside and out; if we wait until they finish building fortifications and live off the grain of the various counties, defeating them will truly be difficult.
proposals.reason: Literal English misspells the biography subject's established name Buyantiemuer as Buyantemuer.

proposals.before: Xingji from youth served in Emperor Renzong's hidden residence and was known for keen intelligence.
proposals.after: Xingji from youth served in Emperor Renzong's residence before accession and was known for keen intelligence.
proposals.reason: 潜邸 denotes a prince's household before accession, not a literally hidden residence.

proposals.before: Xingji ordered a secret arrest; eighteen wives, concubines, female musicians, and women were found; the case was complete; he was convicted and his property registered; from this the powerful held back their hands and the poor rejoiced.
proposals.after: Xingji ordered a secret arrest; eighteen wives, concubines, female musicians, and women were found; the case was complete; he was convicted and his property confiscated into the registers; from this the powerful held back their hands and the poor rejoiced.
proposals.reason: 籍之 in this judicial context means confiscation of property into official registers, not mere registration.

proposals.before: Xingji's nephew Bohua and several dozen personal guards died fighting.
proposals.after: Xingji's nephew Bobuhua and several dozen personal guards died fighting.
proposals.reason: Chinese 伯不华 is Bobuhua; idiomatic Bohua drops the middle syllable 不.

proposals.before: Xingji's nephew Bohua and several dozen personal guards died with them.
proposals.after: Xingji's nephew Bobuhua and several dozen personal guards died with them.
proposals.reason: Chinese 伯不华 is Bobuhua; literal Bohua drops the middle syllable 不.

proposals.before: He entered court as vice minister of works, associate of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites, and supervising censor; he was transferred to vice minister of revenue, promoted to minister, sent out as commissioner of the Yannan surveillance commission, and promoted five times to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
proposals.after: He entered court as vice minister of works, associate of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites, and supervising censor; he was transferred to vice minister of revenue, promoted to minister, sent out as commissioner of the Yannan surveillance commission, and after five further transfers became vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
proposals.reason: 又五迁为 means after five further transfers he became the office, not that he was promoted five times into that same office.

proposals.before: He entered as Vice Minister of Works, Associate of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites, appointed Supervising Censor, transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, promoted to Minister, sent out as Commissioner of the Yannan Surveillance Commission, and five times promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
proposals.after: He entered as Vice Minister of Works, Associate of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Rites, appointed Supervising Censor, transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, promoted to Minister, sent out as Commissioner of the Yannan Surveillance Commission, and after five further transfers became Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
proposals.reason: 又五迁为 means after five further transfers he became the office, not five promotions to that office.

proposals.before: They therefore resolved to dispatch five hundred troops under guard officers Halazhang, Xindu, and Qie to suppress the rebels and report afterward.
proposals.after: They therefore resolved to dispatch five hundred troops under guard officers Halazhang, Xindu, and Qielai to suppress the rebels and report afterward.
proposals.reason: Chinese 怯来 is Qielai; idiomatic Qie truncates the name.

proposals.before: They therefore resolved to dispatch five hundred troops, sending guard officers Halazhang, Xindu, and Qie to suppress them and then report.
proposals.after: They therefore resolved to dispatch five hundred troops, sending guard officers Halazhang, Xindu, and Qielai to suppress them and then report.
proposals.reason: Chinese 怯来 is Qielai; literal Qie truncates the name.

proposals.before: By autumn the court appointed Yirenzhenban left chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and Huonichi left chancellor, both leading troops to Jiangxi.
proposals.after: By autumn the court appointed Yirenzhenban left chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and Huonichi left vice chancellor, both leading troops to Jiangxi.
proposals.reason: Chinese distinguishes 左丞相 (Yirenzhenban) from 左丞 (Huonichi); rendering both as “left chancellor” conflates two different offices.

proposals.before: By autumn the court appointed Yirenzhenban Left Chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and Huonichi Left Chancellor, both leading troops to Jiangxi.
proposals.after: By autumn the court appointed Yirenzhenban Left Chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and Huonichi Left Vice Chancellor, both leading troops to Jiangxi.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 左丞相 for Yirenzhenban and 左丞 for Huonichi; both English fields wrongly use the higher office title for Huonichi.
